# Walk-In Tubs for Elderly

> A family guide for adult children deciding with an aging parent about bathroom safety and walk-in tubs. Published by Aging Safely Baths & More, LLC (Aging Safely Baths), a walk-in tub and roll-in shower supplier and installer serving all 50 U.S. states, with supply-only delivery to Canada. Phone 1-888-779-2284, email sales@agingsafelybaths.com. BBB accredited (A+) since 2012.

This site covers the caregiver side of the decision: noticing warning signs, raising the subject, paying as a family, managing from a distance, and a shared checklist. Buyer's guides written for seniors themselves are on seniorwalkinbathtubs.com; disability and wheelchair-accessible tubs are on handicapbathtubs.com; quotes and installation are handled by agingsafelybaths.com.

## Guides
- [Walk-In Tubs for Elderly Parents: A Family Guide](https://walkintubsforelderly.com/): For adult children deciding with an aging parent: warning signs, how to raise the subject, paying as a family, deciding from a distance, and a checklist.
- [Signs Bathing Is No Longer Safe for an Elderly Parent](https://walkintubsforelderly.com/signs-bathing-is-unsafe/): The warning signs that a parent's tub or shower has become a fall risk, what each sign means, and what to do next. Based on CDC STEADI and NIA guidance.
- [How to Talk to a Parent About Bathroom Safety](https://walkintubsforelderly.com/talk-to-parent-about-bathroom-safety/): How to raise bathroom safety and a walk-in tub with an aging parent without a fight: opening lines, what not to say, involving siblings, and handling a no.
- [Paying for a Parent's Walk-In Tub as a Family](https://walkintubsforelderly.com/paying-for-a-walk-in-tub/): How families pay for a parent's walk-in tub: splitting costs, IRS Publication 502 rules on medical home improvements, long-term care insurance, VA and Medicaid.
- [Long-Distance Caregiving: Bathroom Safety From Afar](https://walkintubsforelderly.com/long-distance-caregiving/): How to make a parent's bathroom safer when you live far away: what to check on visits, getting quotes by photo, measuring by video call, and installation day.
- [Walk-In Tub Family Decision Checklist (Printable)](https://walkintubsforelderly.com/family-decision-checklist/): A printable checklist for families deciding on a walk-in tub or shower for a parent: signs, the talk, assessment, quotes, paying, and installation day.
- [How to Help an Elderly Parent Bathe Safely and With Dignity](https://walkintubsforelderly.com/blog-helping-elderly-parent-bathe-safely.html): A caregiver's guide to helping a parent bathe: room setup, privacy, the risky moment after the bath, useful equipment, and caring for yourself.
- [Walk-In Tub Features That Matter When You Help a Parent](https://walkintubsforelderly.com/blog-walk-in-tub-features-for-elderly-parents.html): The walk-in tub features to compare when a family member will help with bathing: door swing, seat height, grab bars, controls, drain time, and room to assist.
- [Are Hydrotherapy Jets Worth It in a Parent's Walk-In Tub?](https://walkintubsforelderly.com/blog-hydrotherapy-for-elderly.html): Should the family pay extra for hydrotherapy jets in a parent's walk-in tub? Questions for the doctor, cost and funding trade-offs, and when to skip them.

## Key facts (checked 2026-10-15)
- Aging Safely Baths quotes fully installed walk-in tubs at about $15,250 to $20,000 after current promotions, itemized in writing; supply-only delivery is also available.
- IRS Publication 502 (2025 returns): home improvements whose main purpose is medical care can be medical expenses, reduced by any increase in home value; bathroom modifications for a disability are listed as generally not increasing value. Only expenses above 7.5% of AGI count, and only if you itemize. Publication 502 does not list a doctor's recommendation as a requirement for capital expenses, though a doctor's letter is good documentation.
- VA HISA: lifetime benefit up to $6,800 (service-connected, or 50%+ rated) or $2,000; needs a VA physician prescription; excludes spa, hot tub and Jacuzzi-type tubs; roll-in showers are a listed example.
- Original Medicare does not list walk-in tubs as durable medical equipment; some Medicare Advantage plans and state Medicaid waivers may help.
- About 28% (16.2 million) of adults 65+ living in the community lived alone in 2023, including 42% of women 75+ (ACL 2023 Profile of Older Americans).
- More than one in four adults 65+ fall each year, and fewer than half tell their doctor (CDC).

## Safety language
No bathing product removes the risk of a fall. Walk-in tubs and showers are designed to lower risk when installed and used properly.
